subject: Azure PC: signal routing and shadow-account clearing for Contoso engagement
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@microsoft.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T15:12:00Z
Subject: Intro + Contoso co-sell signals / PC referral question

Hi Grace / Vanessa / Ben,

Thanks for hopping on the call last week. Contoso has confirmed interest in a proof-of-concept for multi-region inference (their manufacturing analytics team). I ran the scenario by the field team and they flagged two potential complications that affect Partner Center referral routing:

- Contoso has a set of "shadow" accounts (subsidiaries & BU-owned tenant aliases) in their CRM that are currently not tiled to any MS seller.
- Some of the accounts show pre-existing marketplace listings under a partner ID that predates our conversation.

Can Redwood confirm: if we open a PC referral for the top-level Contoso account, will Partner Center correctly route to the field seller if some of the invoice/tenant aliases live under different account IDs? We want to avoid duplicate seller assignment (and orphaned referrals).

I've looped in Alejandro (Contoso AM) so he can share the account inventory. If useful, we can start with a small subset of five pilot accounts to establish ownership before we open any large-scale referrals.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Microsoft Azure Partner PM — ISV Co-sell
(elena.rossi@microsoft.com)

---

(attachment: contoso_account_inventory_v2.xlsx)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@microsoft.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro + Contoso co-sell signals / PC referral question

Elena — thanks for the context and for attaching the inventory. Looping through:

Short answer: yes, Partner Center routes from the account-level identity that matches the buyer tenant tied to the referral, but gaps in account stitching (shadow aliases) are the main root cause of duplicate/referral misses. We typically recommend a two-step approach for Contoso-type orgs:

1) Shadow-account reconciliation: normalize Contoso tenant aliases to a single canonical account ID in a mapping table. We can script a lightweight reconciliation against the Microsoft tenant list and Contoso CRM fields.
2) Pilot referrals: open PC referrals for the canonical accounts only for the 5 pilot tenants Alejandro suggested so we can validate seller attribution in Microsoft telemetry before scaling.

I'll attach a draft mapping CSV with the column layout we need (canonical_id, tenant_alias, crm_account_id, suggested_seller). Vanessa / Ben — can you review the suggested seller assignments and confirm who will act as the owner for each pilot?

Plan: once owners are agreed, we'll:
- finalize mapping and upload to our shared Drive (link below)
- instruct Contoso to use the canonical tenant for the referral payload
- open the Partner Center referrals for the pilot accounts and monitor attribution for 72 hours

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Partner GTM — Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

(attachment: redwood_account-mapping-draft.csv)

Subject: Re: Intro + Contoso co-sell signals / PC referral question

Thanks Grace — this is helpful. Couple of clarifying points before Vanessa/Ben allocate owners:

- Alejandro: can you confirm which tenant Contoso will use for billing/marketplace? The inventory spreadsheet is useful but has ~18 aliases; we want to be sure the canonical tenant is billing-enabled in Partner Center.
- Microsoft telemetry: when a referral arrives, Partner Center looks at the buyer tenant and the associated Azure AD tenant ID. If the buyer tenant ID maps to a tiled MS seller it will route accordingly. The concern is when Contoso's buyer tenant uses an alias that maps to a different CRM account — that creates split signals.

I'm forwarding Alejandro's quick note below with the Contoso take.

> -----Forwarded message-----
> From: Alejandro Cruz <alejandro.cruz@contoso.com>
> Date: Wed, Jun 9, 2027 at 16:02
> Subject: Re: account list for co-sell pilot
> To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@microsoft.com>
> 
> Hi all — we've attached the canonical billing tenant in the spreadsheet; the top-level Contoso Manufacturing tenant is billed under tenant ID: 55d3-9a1f. The other aliases are BU-level subscriptions that are used for dev/test and are not billing tenants.
> 
> We are happy to surface the five pilot billing tenants and have our procurement team approve the referral flow.
> 
> Alejandro Cruz
> Account Manager, Contoso Manufacturing
> (alejandro.cruz@contoso.com)

Appreciate it — once Vanessa/Ben confirm the seller assignments we'll ask Contoso to submit the referral payload against tenant ID 55d3-9a1f.

Thanks,
Elena

Elena / Alejandro — thanks for the clarification and the tenant ID. Ben and I synced and agreed on seller ownership for the five pilot accounts:

- Contoso Manufacturing (tenant 55d3-9a1f) — seller: Ben Carter (field seller, Midwest)
- Contoso DevLab (alias dev.contoso.com) — seller: Unassigned (will not be part of pilot)
- Contoso IoT BU (alias iot.contoso.com) — seller: Ben Carter
- Contoso QA (alias qa.contoso.com) — seller: Ben Carter
- Contoso EU research (alias eu-research.contoso.com) — seller: Vanessa Ortiz (EMEA field liaise)

Next steps we will take (this week):
1) I will upload the finalized mapping to our shared Drive and attach the cleaned CSV here.
2) We will ask Contoso to submit the Partner Center referral using tenant ID 55d3-9a1f for the top-level account and the canonical tenant for each pilot.
3) Redwood will monitor attribution in the Partner Center telemetry and the Redwood Console for 72 hours and report any misroutes.

I've attached the final mapping and a short checklist for Contoso procurement. If everything looks good, Alejandro — can your procurement team flag when the referral is submitted so we can watch for the telemetry?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Partnerships Manager — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
